skill.name: adaptive-classifier
skill.description: Build, update and honestly evaluate text classifiers with the open-source adaptive-classifier library, which learns new examples and new classes without retraining from scratch. Use for small labeled sets, label sets that change over time, and routing, intent or moderation tasks; not for large static datasets where standard fine-tuning is better.
skill.summary: Guidance for building incremental text classifiers, adding labels, and evaluating performance with held-out data.
skill.author: lambdasec

content.user_title: Build and Evaluate Adaptive Text Classifiers
content.value_statement: Small labeled datasets and changing categories make text classification difficult to maintain. This skill guides incremental classifier updates and held-out evaluation with the adaptive-classifier library.
actual_capabilities: Guides installation checks and API signature inspection for adaptive-classifier.
Provides examples for single-text, batch, and multilabel predictions.
Explains incremental example updates, new classes, and class statistics.
Defines held-out evaluation with baselines, per-class metrics, calibration checks, and order-sensitivity testing.
Documents local save and load workflows, ONNX options, and download approval requirements.
Explains strategic prediction modes and robustness evaluation for adversarial text.
limitations: Requires the adaptive-classifier library; the skill does not install it automatically.
Documents version 0.2.0; model-dependent examples were not executed by the skill author.
Model weights may require approved downloads, and classification quality depends on the encoder and labeled examples.
Updates can change earlier predictions; scores are not guaranteed probabilities, and high-stakes decisions require human review.

use_cases.title: Route changing support intents
use_cases.description: Build a ticket classifier from labeled examples, add emerging intents, and reevaluate existing categories after updates.

use_cases.title: Evaluate small classification datasets
use_cases.description: Compare an adaptive classifier against simple baselines using held-out data, per-class metrics, and learning curves.

use_cases.title: Assess moderation triage robustness
use_cases.description: Explore multilabel predictions and strategic robustness for moderation queues while retaining human review for consequential decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Check whether the library fits
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether adaptive-classifier fits my ticket-routing task with 20 labeled examples per class. Identify missing information and ask before downloading anything.

prompt_templates.title: Build a first classifier
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my labeled texts to draft a local intent classifier with held-out evaluation. Check the installed version and request approval before downloading weights.

prompt_templates.title: Add a new category
prompt_templates.prompt: Add my new billing examples to an existing classifier. Check label consistency and compare held-out performance for old and new classes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: update a classifier without overlooking regressions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare configurations and robustness
prompt_templates.prompt: Design validation-only comparisons for pooling, blending weights, ONNX inference, and strategic robustness. Include order sensitivity, calibration, and a final untouched test evaluation.

output_examples.input: Plan a support intent classifier from a small labeled dataset without downloading weights yet.
output: Suitability: a small dataset with changing intents matches the documented use case.
Preparation: check the installed package version and confirm label consistency.
Evaluation: separate training, validation, and test examples before fitting.
Approval needed: confirm the encoder before downloading model weights.
Results: no performance claims are available until evaluation runs.

output_examples.input: Explain what to check after adding a new technical-support category.
output: Confirm that the new label spelling is consistent and the class count changed as expected.
Provide at least 10 labeled examples before relying on the new class.
Reevaluate held-out examples for both existing and new categories.
Report per-class precision, recall, F1, and sample sizes.
Check update-order sensitivity and route uncertain predictions to human review.

best_practices: Separate training, validation, and test data before adding examples, and remove near-duplicates across splits.
Request approval before model downloads, keep remote model code disabled, and publish only when explicitly requested.
Reevaluate all classes after updates and report per-class metrics with sample sizes.
anti_patterns: Evaluating on training examples or tuning settings against the final test split.
Treating blended prediction scores as calibrated probabilities or upstream benchmark figures as guaranteed outcomes.
Automating high-stakes decisions without human review or ignoring regressions after new labels.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does this skill install the library or download models automatically?
faq.answer: No. It directs assistants to check installation, avoid automatic installation, and obtain approval before model or dataset downloads.

faq.question: Can I add categories after creating a classifier?
faq.answer: Yes. Unseen labels create new classes through added examples. Reevaluate existing classes after each update.

faq.question: Does it support multiple labels per text?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers MultiLabelAdaptiveClassifier, prediction thresholds, and label statistics.

faq.question: Are prediction scores reliable probabilities?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Scores blend prototype similarity and classifier outputs. Validate calibration and rejection thresholds on held-out data.

faq.question: Were the model examples tested end to end?
faq.answer: No. The author checked signatures and defaults for version 0.2.0, but read model-dependent behavior from source and documentation without running it.
